newsitem.title: RWANDA: Fresh fighting in and around Zaire city of Goma.
newsitem.headline: Fresh fighting in and around Zaire city of Goma.

text.p: U.N. staff huddled under their desks in the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Friday because of renewed fighting around the centre for regional aid operations.

Peter Kessler, a spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), quoted U.N. officials in Goma as saying that for more than an hour shooting could be clearly heard in Goma and "our staff are sheltering on the floors of their offices".
Kessler, speaking from Nairobi, said U.N. and other aid workers had regrouped at the UNHCR office in the city centre, partly because of the shooting.
In Geneva, UNHCR spokeswoman Ruth Marshall told a briefing the agency had not taken a final decision to evacuate its staff members from Goma.

Goma is the administrative centre for relief operations for 1.1. million Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire. Many of them have been on the run from fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops for at least a week.
UNHCR spokesman Panos Moumtzis in Goma said the refugees now live in a constant state of panic. "At one point yesterday we had refugees on the road walking in both directions," said Moumtzis.
"They are really panicking. They are very scared. They do not know where to go."

Aid officials said refugees from Kahindo camp north of Goma begand arriving on Friday at Mugunga camp, the largest refugee camp in the world with more than 400,000 refugees crammed on to unsuitable terrain.
"The new arrivals from Kahindo looked extremely tired and exhausted," said Kessler.
Thousands of Rwandans fled from the Rwandan town of Gisenyi because of the fighting just across the border in Zaire, a Reuters eyewitness said.
Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings said the town was emptying after three mortar bombs fired from Zaire hit Gisenyi. There was no immediate word of casualties.
The evacuation of Gisenyi was the worst reported instance of the fighting in Zaire affecting life on the Rwandan side of the border.
"Heavy firing is continuing across the border. Now the Zairean fire is coming into Gisenyi, into hills near Gisenyi and west of Goma," he said.
